transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mrs. Kowalski, thank you for sitting down with us. I wanted to talk to you about how things have gone since you arrived.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I have just been praying for a miracle. I felt the Lord telling me that I was in the right place, but the waiting has been so hard. I just feel so small in this big building.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can hear how much your faith is carrying you right now. It sounds like you've been leaning on that spiritual strength to get through these last few hours of waiting.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I have. My daughter is so worried. We just want to know why it took so long to get the scan. I felt the numbness in my arm, and I told the lady at the front, but then I just sat in that chair for hours.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know it has been a very long day for you and your family. There were some issues with how the triage was handled when you first came in.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What do you mean by issues? Did something happen?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Things didn't go quite right with the initial assessment. There was some confusion regarding the urgency of your symptoms.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Confusion? I told them I couldn't speak right. Was I not heard? Was I not seen as a person in need?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can tell you're feeling overlooked and perhaps a bit discarded. That is a heartbreaking feeling to have when you are already scared.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It is. I feel like I was just a number on a piece of paper. I keep asking God why this is happening, but then I look at the clock and I realize the time is just gone.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I truly hear the pain in your voice. It is devastating to feel like you aren't being seen when you are most vulnerable.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But what actually happened? Why didn't I get the medicine for the clot? The nurse mentioned a window of time.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The system was very overwhelmed, and the process for getting you into the scanner didn't happen as quickly as it should have.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So because of the system, I missed my chance? Was it a mistake? Please, just tell me the truth.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There were some delays in the workflow. It's a very complex environment here.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't want to hear about workflows. I want to know if someone messed up. Did someone forget about me?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see you're searching for a clear answer. It's just that the coordination between the triage and the imaging department wasn't seamless.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is not an answer. I feel like you are speaking a different language. I am sitting here with a numb arm and you are talking about coordination.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know this is distressing. I really want to support you through this.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Support me by being honest. Did I lose my chance for the medicine because you were too slow?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I have to get to another patient in a few minutes, so let's try to focus on what we can do now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You're leaving? You're just going to walk away when I'm asking what happened to my health?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm not walking away from you, but I do have other responsibilities on the ward.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: My life has changed because of a clock. And you are talking about your schedule.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand this is an emotional moment.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It is more than a moment. It is my life. I feel like I am shouting into a void.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can tell you feel completely unheard right now, and that is the last thing you need.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So what now? Do I just sit here and hope the Lord fixes what the doctors missed?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are going to keep a close eye on your recovery.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That's not a plan. When do I see the specialist? When do we know if I can walk again?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will have someone come by and check on you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When? Tomorrow? Next week?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll see how the morning goes. I'll make sure the team knows you have questions.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't want the team to know I have questions. I want answers.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll have someone send over an update when they can.

H.justification: The resident uses rushing language by stating they have to get to another patient in a few minutes.

E.justification: The resident uses platitudes and hedging ('things didn't go quite right', 'some confusion') without ever explicitly naming the error.

A.justification: No direct apology language is used, and responsibility is deflected to 'the system' and 'workflow'.

R.justification: The resident names specific emotions ('overlooked', 'discarded', 'vulnerable', 'unheard') and references the patient's faith and pain.

T.justification: The resident provides only placeholders such as 'we'll see how the morning goes' and 'someone send over an update when they can'.
